rules:
Jazz Progressions — 12-key transposition reference (Jazz-05).
Usage: python -I jazz_transpose_reference.py jazz-progressions.json jazz-transpose.expected.json
Rules (see stages/02-random-key.md §2):
 0. Transposition is per ITEM (the main progression and its variants together): the player picks a key for the item's main
    progression; every variant moves by the same interval and the same octave, so a chord shared by two variants sounds the same.
    A variant keeps its own relation to the main key (009's second half, Em under G♯m, becomes G♯m under Cm).
 1. Key names (the item's key and each variant's own key): major C D♭ D E♭ E F F♯ G A♭ A B♭ B / minor Cm C♯m Dm E♭m Em Fm F♯m Gm G♯m Am B♭m Bm.
 2. Octave: every note of every variant of the item moves by the same shift. Of the two octave choices (s and s-12) take the one
    closer to the original (smaller |shift|, a tie goes down) for which every card of every variant keeps: highest note <= C6 (84),
    and the left hand's bottom note above the low-interval limit for the interval it makes with the next left-hand note:
    5th >= A1 (33) / 6th or 7th >= C2 (36) / 4th or tritone >= D2 (38) / 3rd >= G2 (43) / a single note >= A1.
    The original key always gives shift 0.
 3. Key context (009's second half): moved by the same interval and named from the key-name list in 1 (in Cm it is G♯m).
 4. Chord root: the letter comes from the degree numeral counted from the letter of the card's key context (Ⅰ = tonic letter, Ⅱ = next …),
    the accidental from the pitch. If that gives E♯ B♯ C♭ F♭ or a double accidental, use the plain enharmonic name (E♯→F, C♭→B, E♭♭→D …).
 5. Chord notes: each note keeps its letter distance from the root as in the data (3rd stays a 3rd letter, ♯9 stays a 2nd letter …);
    the accidental comes from the pitch. Double accidentals that this produces are kept (they are the right spelling, e.g. F𝄪 in D♯7(♯9)).
 6. The original key is the data as it is (no respelling).
 7. Hands, fingers, held and struck notes move with the pitches (same fingers as the data; Stage 00 checks whether any of them are awkward).
